doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Pop music of the 1940s-50s and the albums Hank recorded
summary: Monk asks what popular music impressed Hank as a teenager; Hank answers by listing albums and artists he recorded, including Tapestry, Peggy Lee, A&M and Lou Adler acts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Because I’ve been reading about you and I say oh, I wanted to be in the booth for that and you could just think of so many moments. I’d like to put — imagine you at age oh somewhere between age 13 and 14 and I was looking at the pop songs, the top popular songs of those years. And I see things like Doris Day “Sentimental Journey” and Perry Como “Prisoner of Love.” And if we kept going we’d arrive at “Rock Around the Clock” and Elvis Presley. So my question, what was it in popular music being played on the radio do you recall anything in particular that really made an impression on you?
Oh are you talking about records that I’ve heard that I wanted to —

Oh gosh there were so many in those days. I’ve a name blockage but there were so many albums, albums that I did, “Tapestry,” “Rhymes and Reasons.” In all those days I really loved the big bands, I mean I really loved doing a lot of those. I recorded so many great artists over my career: Shorty Rodgers, Peggy Lee, the Lennon Sisters, I mean I worked for A&M Records for several years. I worked for Lou Adler, Merry Clayton, Gene McDaniels albums, “The Rocky Horror Show,” stuff like that.
